question: In free generation on one science question (12), does loading the 316 core tensors as BF16 change how long K4-Core-K6 replies on the vLLM fork with route b?
statement: Ratio of geometric-mean completion tokens, BF16 core / 6-bit core, 0.80 [0.51, 1.14] on question 12, 12 samples per arm; the interval includes 1 and is wider than the frozen band of 0.8 to 1.25, so the frozen reading is inconclusive. This is the only free-generation length measurement on science questions in these runs: one question, one engine.
quantity: exp(mean log completion tokens | all - mean log completion tokens | k6)
sign: ratio below 1 = the BF16 core wrote shorter replies
n: 12 per arm, seeds 51201-51212 in both arms; one launch per arm
interval: 95% bootstrap, 2,000 replicates resampling samples within each arm, seed 20261103 (analyze_g4.py)

evidence.text:
- Primary: delta = mean(log completion tokens | all) - mean(log completion tokens | k6), 95% bootstrap interval

- A shift is detected when the interval excludes 0. "No shift of 1.25x or more" when the interval lies inside
  +-log(1.25). Anything else is inconclusive.

bound: a ratio from 0.51 to 1.14 (BF16 core / 6-bit core) is not excluded
